\chapter{Chapter02 — Edge Isoperimetric}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter02.TotalInfluence.EdgeIsoperimetric
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter02.TotalInfluence.EdgeIsoperimetric}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Probability of a positive value]
\lean{FABL.positiveProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b005}
\label{FABL.positiveProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.uniformProbability}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its positive probability is
the uniform probability that $f(x)=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of positive probability]
\lean{FABL.positiveProbability_nonneg}
\label{FABL.positiveProbability_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.positiveProbability, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For any function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, the uniform probability that $f$ equals $1$
is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound on positive probability]
\lean{FABL.positiveProbability_le_one}
\label{FABL.positiveProbability_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.positiveProbability, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For any function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, the uniform probability that $f$ equals $1$
is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive probability under coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.positiveProbability_cons}
\label{FABL.positiveProbability_cons}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.expect_fin_cons, FABL.firstCoordinateRestriction, FABL.positiveProbability, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\{-1,1\}$. The uniform probability that $f$ equals $1$ is the
average of the corresponding probabilities for the two restrictions obtained by fixing
the first coordinate to $1$ and to $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Difference of positive probabilities]
\lean{FABL.abs_positiveProbability_sub_le_uniformProbability_ne}
\label{FABL.abs_positiveProbability_sub_le_uniformProbability_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.positiveProbability, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f,g:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$. Under the uniform
distribution on the cube, write $P_+(f)$ for the probability that $f(x)=1$. Then
$|P_+(f)-P_+(g)|$ is at most the probability that $f(x)\ne g(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary entropy lower bound]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy_of_le_half}
\label{FABL.two_mul_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy_of_le_half}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $p$ with $0\le p\le \tfrac12$, the binary entropy satisfies
$2p\log 2\le -p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$, with the usual continuous convention at the
endpoints.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary entropy lower bound]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_min_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy}
\label{FABL.two_mul_min_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.two_mul_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy_of_le_half}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $p$ with $0\le p\le1$, $2\min(p,1-p)\log 2\le H(p)$, where
$H(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$ is the binary entropy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary entropy and distance from balance]
\lean{FABL.one_le_binEntropy_div_log_two_add_abs}
\label{FABL.one_le_binEntropy_div_log_two_add_abs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.two_mul_min_mul_log_two_le_binEntropy}
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $p$ with $0\le p\le 1$, the binary entropy satisfies $1\le
H(p)/\log 2+|2p-1|$, where $H(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$ with the usual endpoint
convention.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Midpoint logarithmic inequality]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_midpoint_mul_logb_inv_le}
\label{FABL.two_mul_midpoint_mul_logb_inv_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.one_le_binEntropy_div_log_two_add_abs}
\difficulty{6}
For nonnegative real numbers $a$ and $b$, twice their arithmetic mean multiplied by the
base-$2$ logarithm of the reciprocal of their arithmetic mean is at most the sum of $a$
times the base-$2$ logarithm of $1/a$, $b$ times the base-$2$ logarithm of $1/b$, and
$|a-b|$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Write $p$ for the
probability that $f=1$ under the uniform distribution on the cube, and let $I(f)$ be the
sum over coordinates of the uniform expectation of the squared discrete derivative of
$f$. Then $2p\log_2(1/p)\le I(f)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Probability of a negative value]
\lean{FABL.negativeProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b005}
\label{FABL.negativeProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.uniformProbability}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its negative probability is
the uniform probability that $f(x)=-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positive probability of the negated function]
\lean{FABL.positiveProbability_neg}
\label{FABL.positiveProbability_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.negativeProbability, FABL.positiveProbability, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For any function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, the uniform probability that $-f$ equals $1$
is the uniform probability that $f$ equals $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real-valued representation of negation]
\lean{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal_neg}
\label{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign
cube to $\\{\pm1\}$. The real-valued function associated with the pointwise negation of
$f$ is the pointwise negative of the real-valued function associated with $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Minority probability]
\lean{FABL.minorityProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p052-b007}
\label{FABL.minorityProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.negativeProbability, FABL.positiveProbability}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its minority probability is
the smaller of the uniform probabilities that its value is $1$ and that its value is
$-1$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Write $p$ for the
smaller of the probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $-1$, under the uniform
distribution on the cube, and let $I(f)$ be the sum over coordinates of the uniform
expectation of the squared discrete derivative of $f$. Then $2p\log_2(1/p)\le I(f)$.
\end{theorem}
